quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow circular traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow shows.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and be ready to stop when you see it.

questions.question: What does the posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a suggested driving speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The highest safe speed when conditions are good.
The highest safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed when conditions are good.
questions.explanation: The speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road when conditions are ideal. You may need to drive slower when weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is coming up.
You are near a construction area.
You must turn left soon.
The road will become narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will become narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line at the edge of the road marks where the road ends. When this line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get their attention. If they do not move, steer to the right to escape. Do not swerve left because they may correct at the last second and you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the crash impact.

questions.question: When turning onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?

options.text: Always the right lane.
Always the left lane.
The lane that will cause the most traffic problems.
The lane that will cause the least traffic problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane that will cause the least traffic problems.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that interferes least with other traffic. Do not make a dangerous turn into traffic.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit when entering the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's weight may make it hard to turn. Slowing down first helps you stay in control.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Keep them straight and set the parking brake.
Turn them away from the curb.
Turn them toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop next to the car in front of your parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the car in front of your parking space.
questions.explanation: After checking traffic and signaling, pull up next to the front car. Then turn your wheels and park.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic going in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. It tells drivers what they must do. This sign means parking is not allowed here.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: On a multilane road with traffic moving in opposite directions, how should you use the shared center lane?

options.text: To pass another vehicle
To slow down or stop before turning left
As a through-traffic lane when traffic is slow
As a parking lane

questions.correctAnswerText: To slow down or stop before turning left
questions.explanation: Use the center lane only when you need to slow down or stop to make a safe left turn. Never use it to pass or to continue driving through.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop and look, then go if the road is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: Shared lanes are for:

options.text: Bicyclists.
Truck drivers.
Motorcyclists.
Passenger vehicle operators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicyclists.
questions.explanation: Shared lanes are for bicyclists. They help bicycles stay safe in narrow lanes and alert drivers that bicyclists may be in the lane.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the emergency vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and give other traffic the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give other traffic the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let traffic on the road you are entering go first.

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. You should:

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and go through.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through.

questions.question: You cannot pass other vehicles within ____ of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.

options.text: 200 feet
100 feet
500 feet
350 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Do not pass within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you just came from. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. They are controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: A second train could be coming on the other track. Wait until you are sure no train is approaching on either track before crossing.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid yellow lines cannot be crossed, except when you are turning.

questions.question: If a vehicle coming toward you is using high beams, where should you look?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: All car crashes must be reported within how many days?

options.text: Five

questions.explanation: If no police officer investigates your crash and no one is injured or killed, you must file a written report within 10 days.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Accelerate to the speed of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match the highway traffic. Signal, check for an opening, then merge safely.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Get out and check behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is backed up. Wait until there is space on the other side so you can clear the intersection completely.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This helps you see your blind spots.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed to reach your destination faster.
Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop safely.
